title: Pinching and block direct sums
subtitle: G2 lecture 060000 · expanded companion
adaptation: Standalone slide treatment of the spoken lecture and display-only mathematical appendix; authored derivations, worked calculations and local SVG diagrams.

slides.title: Remove coupling between orthogonal pieces
slides.lead: Pinching keeps diagonal blocks of an operator and discards its off-diagonal blocks.
body: Split a Hilbert space H as M⊕M⊥ and let P project onto M. Relative to this decomposition, A has four blocks: two diagonal actions and two off-diagonal couplings.
The pinching map retains the action within each piece but deletes the transitions between them. The fundamental theorem is that this deletion cannot increase any unitarily invariant norm.
slides.takeaway: Pinching deletes coupling while keeping the diagonal blocks.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 060000 · Remove coupling between orthogonal pieces

slides.title: Write the four operator blocks
slides.lead: Block notation makes the geometry of pinching explicit.
body: PAP acts within M; (I−P)A(I−P) acts within M⊥. The blocks PA(I−P) and (I−P)AP carry vectors across the decomposition.
Thus the pinched matrix is block diagonal. This operation is not the same as a compression to M, which keeps only one of the diagonal blocks and loses the other.
slides.takeaway: Both diagonal blocks survive; only off-diagonal coupling disappears.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 060000 · Write the four operator blocks

slides.title: Build the block-sign reflection
slides.lead: The reflection J=2P−I acts by +1 on M and by −1 on M⊥.
body: It is self-adjoint and squares to the identity, hence it is unitary. Conjugation by J leaves A₁₁ and A₂₂ unchanged while reversing the signs of A₁₂ and A₂₁.
Averaging the original matrix with its conjugate cancels the off-diagonal blocks, exactly producing the pinching map.
slides.takeaway: Reflection averaging gives a short coordinate-free proof of the block formula.

slides.title: Prove pinching is contractive
slides.lead: Let ||·||Φ be any unitarily invariant norm on this fixed square-matrix space.
body: By the triangle inequality, the norm of (A+JAJ)/2 is at most (||A||Φ+||JAJ||Φ)/2. Unitary invariance makes ||JAJ||Φ=||A||Φ.
Therefore the pinching norm cannot exceed the original. The same proof works separately for each Ky Fan sum and every Schatten norm.
slides.takeaway: Triangle inequality plus unitary invariance proves every pinching contraction.

slides.title: Check a two-by-two example
slides.lead: The matrix A=[[3,4],[4,3]] has singular values 7 and 1.
body: Pinch onto the coordinate axes. The off-diagonal fours disappear and the result is diag(3,3), with singular values 3 and 3.

The operator norm drops from 7 to 3 and the nuclear norm drops from 8 to 6. Yet the second singular value rises from 1 to 3, showing again why a universal componentwise singular-value inequality is too strong.
slides.takeaway: Pinching contracts every Ky Fan sum without decreasing each singular value separately.

slides.title: Ky Fan sums express a stronger conclusion
slides.lead: The same contraction holds for every k, not merely for one selected matrix norm.
body: Because each Ky Fan k-sum is itself unitarily invariant and satisfies the triangle inequality, the reflection argument yields Kₖ(Π_P(A))≤Kₖ(A) for all k.
Equivalently, the singular-value list of the pinched operator is weakly majorized by that of A. The dominance of all symmetric gauges follows from majorization theory.
slides.takeaway: Pinching yields a full weak-majorization statement.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 060000 · Ky Fan sums express a stronger conclusion

slides.title: A direct sum uses a different formula
slides.lead: If A and B act on separate orthogonal spaces, the block diagonal map A⊕B contains the singular values of both.
body: The source Gram operator is (A*A)⊕(B*B), whose eigenvalues combine the eigenvalues of the two Gram operators. Taking square roots concatenates their singular-value lists, with any necessary zeros.
The concatenation—not ordinary addition—determines the norms of a direct sum.
slides.takeaway: Direct-sum singular values concatenate rather than add pointwise.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 060000 · A direct sum uses a different formula

slides.title: Schatten p-norms of block sums
slides.lead: For finite p, Schatten norms add after taking the pth power; the operator norm uses a maximum.
body: Summing the pth powers over the concatenated singular-value list immediately separates into the contribution of A and the contribution of B.
For p=2 this is the familiar Pythagorean addition of squared Frobenius norms. For p=∞ the largest singular value belongs to one of the two blocks.
slides.takeaway: Schatten power sums are additive on orthogonal direct sums.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 060000 · Schatten p-norms of block sums

slides.title: Pinching versus assembling blocks
slides.lead: Pinching begins with a coupled operator and deletes the off-diagonal blocks.
body: A direct sum begins with independent operators on separate spaces and builds a larger block diagonal operator. The first has a contractive inequality; the second has an exact singular-value concatenation identity.
Keeping these constructions distinct is important when moving between selected and complementary spectral subspaces in a perturbation argument.
slides.takeaway: One operation removes coupling; the other combines already-independent operators.

slides.title: Rebuild the reflection proof
slides.lead: Write the four blocks of A relative to a projector P, then calculate JAJ for J=2P−I.
body: Show that the average cancels the off-diagonal entries. Apply the triangle inequality and unitary invariance of a chosen gauge to obtain the pinching bound.
Finally compute singular values of A⊕B from the Gram direct sum and derive both the finite-p Schatten identity and the operator-norm maximum formula.
slides.takeaway: Reflection averaging and Gram block sums are the two reusable calculations.
